title: 5.10.4 Sub-build: Gravity and a tap
description: A bird falls. One tap sends it back up. Build that alone, before there are pipes.

steps.title: Run it first
steps.instructions: The bird falls and lands on the ground. Nothing stops it and no key does anything.

steps.title: Turn gravity on
steps.instructions: In `setup()`, set `world.gravity.y = 10;`. Run it: the bird falls faster and faster, because gravity adds speed every frame.
hints: Gravity is a number on the world, not on the sprite.
Zero gravity means nothing falls; that is the default.

steps.title: Tap to flap
steps.instructions: On `kb.presses('space')`, set `bird.vel.y = -5;`. A negative `vel.y` is up on screen, so each tap replaces the fall with a climb.
hints: Use `presses`, not `pressing`: holding Space should not be a rocket.
Try -4, -6 and -8 and describe how each feels.

requirements.title: Gravity is on
requirements.description: The world has gravity above 0, so sprites fall. Help: 5.2.6 (Reading: Gravity)

requirements.title: A tap goes up
requirements.description: A key press sets a negative vel.y, so the bird climbs. Help: 5.1.15 (Reading: Velocity: vel.x and vel.y)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a short moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: Gravity and a tap". The task: turn gravity on in setup() and set the bird's vel.y to a negative number on a key press, so one tap reverses a fall. This is a sub-build: a small isolated program whose only job is this one mechanic. Accept any names, helpers, arrow functions and ternaries. A line only in a comment or string does not count. Use short, plain notes for a 14-year-old, name their own line when something is missing, never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Gravity is on
rubric.description: world.gravity.y is set above 0 in setup().

rubric.title: The tap is an impulse
rubric.description: The key press sets vel.y to a negative number (or applies an upward force); it does not set y directly.
